subject: AtlasAI production: latency & 5xx spike — SLA compensation and contract amendment
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@atlasai.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate and latency impacting AtlasAI production (Aug 24)

Hi Olga,

We observed a significant regression on our Redwood-powered endpoints between 14:18 and 15:30 PT today. Key customer impact:
- p95 latency jumped to ~2.2s (our expected p95 ~200–300ms)
- 5xx error rate spiked to 3.8% (typical <0.1%)
- End-to-end throughput observed to drop ~40% (from ~1,200 rps down to ~720 rps) for ~72 minutes

This affected multiple downstream customers and caused several failed inference requests. We're past the point of triage and need:
1) a short summary of what happened and mitigations taken (for our execs)
2) a proposed SLA credit or remediation (per section 5.2 of our contract)
3) a timeline for a formal postmortem and any contract changes to prevent recurring events

Please treat this as high priority and loop in whoever you need. Procurement and contracts are cc'ed. I attached a small set of request IDs and timestamps we pulled from our side.

Attachments: Atlas_SLA_Failure_Log_20260824.csv (CSV, 2MB)

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, AtlasAI
sara@atlasai.com

Sara — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're actively investigating and I've opened an internal incident. Preliminary notes: we saw correlated GPU throttling events in one AZ combined with cache cold-starts during the surge window.

Can we hop on a 30-min sync now or at 16:00 PT? I want to:
- confirm the affected routes and request IDs
- share our short-term mitigations (failover + cache warming)

I'll share an initial credit estimate after confirming the customer impact and contract terms; we take SLA breaches seriously and will propose an appropriate remediation.

I've attached an internal snapshot (Incident_Timeline_Snapshot_olga_v1.txt) with the events from our side.

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: AtlasAI production spike — credit calc and remediation plan

Team — looping you in; AtlasAI (major enterprise customer, deal ATL-2025-94) experienced a 72-minute window of degraded service that impacted production traffic this afternoon. Key metrics (from Atlas logs + our telemetry):
- window: 2026-08-24 14:18–15:30 PT (~72 minutes)
- p95 latency observed: ~2.2s vs contract SLO p95 <= 300ms
- 5xx rate peak: 3.8% (baseline <0.1%)
- throughput drop: ~40% for the window

Customer wants an explicit credit and a contract amendment that includes a deterministic escalation path and improved rollback guarantees. Options I'm proposing for discussion (we need legal/finance numbers):
1) Financial remediation: prorated credit for the affected billing period — propose a dollar estimate and cap (see attached observability_snapshot.png).
2) Service remediation: one-time operational package (2 weeks of dedicated burst capacity + priority incident support for 90 days) + modest credit.

Please review and provide:
- Sean: a draft credit calculation and language we can propose to procurement/contracts (DocuSign-ready)
- Marissa: ops remediation plan (short-term and follow-up PM) and acceptance criteria for rollback/failsafe
- Jonas/Laura: finance/legal input on limits and precedent for amendment language

Attachments: observability_snapshot.png

Olga
From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: AtlasAI production spike — credit calc and remediation plan

Quick calc and recommendation:
- Contract monthly committed spend: $300,000 (ATL-2025-94)
- Breach duration: 72 minutes (~1.2 hours) inside a single 30-day billing period
- SLA credit policy (baseline): for p95 breach > 60 minutes we typically offer a prorated credit; precedent ranges 5–20% of monthly depending on severity and business impact

Proposed commercial offer to close quickly:
A) One-time credit of 15% of monthly committed spend = $45,000 applied to Aug invoice +
B) Operational offer: complimentary Dedicated burst for 30 days (value-add) + shared remediation review with our infra PMs

Rationale: positions us as accountable, provides tangible $ relief, and buys time while ops implements mitigations. If AtlasAI prefers a pure operational fix (no cash credit), offer B plus a 5% one-month credit.

Attached: credit_workbook.xlsx (workbook with calc and two scenarios). Legal: we should prepare a short amendment template to cover the credit and any SLA changes; include a rollback clause (mandatory canary and auto-failover behavior) and an explicit postmortem SLA timeline.

-sean
From: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlasai.com, contracts@atlasai.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasAI production: latency & 5xx spike — SLA compensation and contract amendment

Olga / Sean — thank you for the quick analysis and the proposed options. Procurement prefers a deterministic dollar credit for reconciliation; finance wants to avoid open-ended operational credits unless tied to explicit SLAs.

Can you send a DocuSign-ready amendment (with the 15% credit callout) and a redlined SLA that clarifies automated rollback and escalation paths? We need the formal paperwork on our desk by COB Fri (2026-08-28) to avoid internal procurement delays. I've attached a short impact summary from our side for the postmortem.

Attachment: AtlasAI_impact_summary.docx

Thanks,
Sara
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@atlasai.com>, procurement@atlasai.com, contracts@atlasai.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasAI production: latency & 5xx spike — SLA compensation and contract amendment

Sara / Atlas procurement team — thanks for the clarity. Per our internal review and Sean's recommendation, Redwood will deliver the following:

1) Commercial remediation (per your preference): one-time credit of 15% of the monthly committed spend (15% of $300,000 = $45,000) applied to the August invoice.

2) Contract amendment: we've prepared a short amendment that documents the credit and adds two updates to the SLA:
   - Deterministic rollback clause: mandatory canary + auto-failover to cached variant for sustained latency spikes > 2x SLO across 3 consecutive p95 windows
   - Postmortem timeline: full postmortem delivered within 7 business days and follow-up remediation plan within 21 business days

3) Operational remediation: Redundant capacity provisioning in the affected AZs, improved cache-warming heuristics, and a joint runbook review with AtlasAI within 5 business days.

Attachments: redwood_remediation_plan_v1.docx, credit_workbook.xlsx
DocuSign link (amendment template): https://docusign.example.com/templates/rdw-sla-amend-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ATL-2025-94

Please confirm that the credit figure and amendment language are acceptable and we'll route the DocuSign for signature today. If procurement needs alternate wording for internal approval, let us know and we can iterate quickly.

Thanks for working through this.

Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
